r.정치 구도: A presidential system in which the president serves a single four-year term. For more than half a century government forces, left-wing guerrillas, right-wing paramilitaries and drug cartels fought a tangled war; in 2016 the largest guerrilla group, the FARC, signed a peace agreement with the government, laid down its weapons and became a political party. In 2022 the country elected its first left-wing president, who promised 'total peace' through talks with the remaining armed groups, but those groups instead expanded their reach. In the June 2026 runoff a right-wing candidate won by little more than one percentage point, swinging power back to the right. The new government says it will end negotiations with armed groups and confront them with military force. Congress is split among many parties, so passing reforms requires building coalitions.

t.why: It grows more coca, the raw material for cocaine, than any other country, which has long made it Washington's key partner in fighting drugs. In 2025 the United States determined that Colombia had failed to meet its counternarcotics obligations, badly straining relations, but the new government that took office in 2026 cut ties with Cuba and joined a US-led security initiative, moving firmly back toward Washington. As neighboring Venezuela's economy collapsed, Colombia took in more people fleeing that country than anywhere else. It is the only South American country with coastlines on both the Caribbean and the Pacific, and its border with Panama makes it the land bridge between North and South America. It was the first Latin American country to become a NATO partner, and as home to part of the Amazon rainforest it has a voice in climate diplomacy.
t.rel: Its border of more than 2,000 km with Venezuela makes armed groups and smuggling major problems. With Ecuador, drug gangs in the border region bring repeated cooperation and friction. It fought Nicaragua at the International Court of Justice over their Caribbean maritime boundary.
t.korea: During the Korean War it was the only Latin American country to send troops, dispatching more than 4,000 soldiers along with warships from 1951, and more than 100 of them were killed. Diplomatic relations were established in March 1962. The two countries' free trade agreement took effect in July 2016, Colombia's first with an Asian country. Korea imports a great deal of Colombian coffee.
t.know: Colombia is one of the world's top flower exporters; many of the flowers in US florists come from there.
etext: Crude oil and coal make up the largest share of exports, so the economy swings with global energy prices. Few new fields have been found and reserves are shrinking, yet the previous government halted new exploration contracts. The government that took office in 2026 says it will allow fracking again.

It sells large amounts of coffee, flowers, bananas and avocados. Its highland climate produces high-quality arabica coffee, and Colombia supplies a large share of the flowers sold in the United States.
Software, call centers and start-ups are growing around Medellin and Bogota. The delivery app Rappi has spread across Latin America.

About half of all workers have no formal contract or social insurance. Armed groups and drug cartels make investment and mining in rural areas difficult, and widening budget deficits have cost the country credit-rating downgrades.
